profile.summary: CMLM designs an amino acid sequence for a protein backbone that is given to it (inverse folding). It is the non-autoregressive ProteinMPNN baseline of the ByProt codebase: a ProteinMPNN-style graph encoder and decoder trained by conditional masked language modelling, so at generation time it predicts every position at once from one categorical distribution rather than one residue after another. The released checkpoint is called protein_mpnn_cmlm and was trained on CATH 4.2.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The model is ProteinMPNN's message-passing encoder and decoder, trained with a conditional masked language modelling objective instead of left-to-right prediction. Generation uses the mask-predict strategy with one decoding iteration by default, so all positions are filled in a single parallel pass. The ByProt defaults make this explicit: max_iter is 1 and the strategy is mask_predict for ProtMPNN-CMLM, against 5 iterations and denoising for LM-Design. Sampling temperature defaults to 0, which makes the output deterministic.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: One checkpoint is released: protein_mpnn_cmlm, trained on CATH 4.2, published in the Zenodo deposit 10046338 of 27 October 2023 alongside the LM-Design checkpoints. A result must name the decoding settings as well as the checkpoint, because the output depends on the number of iterations, the strategy and the temperature. The HyInv report ran it at its published setting, one parallel pass at temperature 0.1, and reports that regenerating the sequences reproduced the released scores to within 0.0022 scTM with all sequences identical.

sections.title: What a third party reports
sections.body: The HyInv report used CMLM as one of ten published baselines on inverse folding panels. It states that the parallel decoders, CMLM among them, sample at much lower diversity than its own model and have the lowest scTM, and its table of paired differences puts HyInv ahead of CMLM by 0.048 scTM on average. These are the HyInv authors' figures for their own comparison, not Rewire's, and not the CMLM developers' claims.

strengths.text: Decoding is one parallel pass, so it is fast: the HyInv report measures 439 ms to design 128 sequences for a 402 residue backbone, against 2,907 ms for ProteinMPNN.

gaps: No parameter count, no architecture sizes and no context limit are published for this checkpoint.
The LM-Design paper was read only as its arXiv abstract, which describes LM-Design and not the CMLM baseline, so nothing here rests on the paper's own account of CMLM.
The method paper the HyInv report cites for CMLM is Ghazvininejad et al. 2019 on mask-predict decoding in machine translation, which was not read and is not a protein model release.
No training configuration details (epochs, hardware, masking rate) were read; they are in the repository's config files, not in the README.

run_guide.summary: Install ByProt, download the CMLM checkpoint and design a sequence for one PDB backbone.
prerequisites: Conda with Python 3.7, as the repository's installation block sets up.
A GPU: the designer example sets cuda=True.
A backbone PDB file. The repository ships examples under data/.
Code is Apache-2.0; the checkpoint on Zenodo is CC BY 4.0.

steps.title: Get the code at the pinned commit
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/BytedProtein/ByProt.git
cd ByProt
git checkout --detach dd279dc85f76ee2c28c819b71bf3911b90159f0a
steps.explanation: The repository is the one the README's checkpoint table belongs to. The clone and the detached checkout were added by Rewire so the later commands match the files read at this commit.

steps.shell:
mkdir -p run/logs/fixedbb/cath_4.2
cd run/logs/fixedbb/cath_4.2
curl -L -o protein_mpnn_cmlm.zip "https://zenodo.org/records/10046338/files/protein_mpnn_cmlm.zip?download=1"
unzip protein_mpnn_cmlm.zip
cd -
steps.explanation: The URL is the checkpoint link from the README's table. The folder layout follows the README's own example path, run/logs/fixedbb/cath_4.2/protein_mpnn_cmlm. The curl, unzip and mkdir lines were written by Rewire; the sources give a download link but no command.
steps.source_locator: ByProt README.md: Pretrained model weights, Example 1 exp_path; Zenodo files list

steps.title: Design a sequence for one backbone
steps.shell:
python3 - <<'PY'
from byprot.utils.config import compose_config as Cfg
from byprot.tasks.fixedbb.designer import Designer

# 1. instantialize designer
exp_path = "run/logs/fixedbb/cath_4.2/protein_mpnn_cmlm"
cfg = Cfg(
    cuda=True,
    generator=Cfg(
        max_iter=1,
        strategy='mask_predict',
        temperature=0,
        eval_sc=False,  
    )
)
designer = Designer(experiment_path=exp_path, cfg=cfg)

# 2. load structure from pdb file
pdb_path = "data/3uat_variants/3uat_GK.pdb"
designer.set_structure(pdb_path)

# 3. generate sequence from the given structure
designer.generate()

# 4. calculate evaluation metircs
designer.calculate_metrics()
PY
steps.explanation: Copied from the README's Example 1, wrapped by Rewire in a shell heredoc, with the two absolute placeholder paths replaced by paths relative to the clone.

notes: The identity of this record needs a human eye. CMLM is not a model released under its own name: the HyInv report cites Ghazvininejad et al. 2019, a machine translation paper on mask-predict decoding, and the released weights are the protein_mpnn_cmlm checkpoint of the ByProt repository, which is the official implementation of LM-Design and presents CMLM as its non-autoregressive ProteinMPNN baseline. This page is written from ByProt and the Zenodo deposit on that basis. A reviewer should decide whether the record belongs beside the LM-Design record, which shares every source here, and whether it also overlaps a ProteinMPNN record. No parameter count, architecture size or length limit is published for the checkpoint. Quotes from the HyInv report come from a pdftotext text layer, so line breaks inside them follow the PDF layout.
